title: Mukesh Singh Chaturvedi v. State of U.P. & Ors.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sanjay Misra, J. and Anant Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; relegated to clause 6.5; bill not interfered with
headnote: A writ challenging a consumption bill, including on the plea that the meter was defective, raises highly disputed questions of fact for the authority holding the connection records under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The High Court will not interfere with the bill and will relegate the consumer to that remedy.
facts: Mukesh Singh Chaturvedi challenged a 20 May 2014 electricity bill issued by Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited. He alleged the meter was defective and the bill could not be raised. The licensee objected that clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnished a complete remedy before the authority holding the connection records, which could decide disputed facts. The Division Bench heard counsel for the petitioner, the State, and Dakshinanchal.

holding_units.holding: A writ challenging an electricity consumption bill, including on the plea that the meter was defective, raises highly disputed questions of fact which the authority holding the connection records must decide under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will not interfere with the bill and will relegate the consumer to that remedy.

not_decided.point: Validity of the 20.05.2014 bill and whether the meter was defective
not_decided.note: Writ court did not examine the bill on merits and left the dispute to the clause 6.5 authority.
